title: BFS with an array and head index
summary: Compute shortest unweighted graph distances with a queue and mark vertices when enqueuing them.
code: func distances(in graph: [Int: [Int]], from start: Int) -> [Int: Int] {
triggers: shortest hop counts in a graph with equal edge weights
minimum number of equal-cost transitions from a start state, with cycles or duplicate edges
prompts: Find reachable vertices and their minimum hop counts, including graphs with cycles.
A transit map gives direct stops with equal travel cost. Compute the fewest hops from one stop to every reachable stop.
invariant: Queued vertices already have their shortest distance and are enqueued only once.
mantra: Visit on enqueue; advance the head; discover one layer at a time.
pitfalls: Array.removeFirst repeatedly shifts elements; a head index avoids that cost.
Marking only on dequeue allows duplicate queue entries.
BFS does not solve general weighted shortest paths.

anchors.name: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
anchors.trick: Treat valid cells as vertices and legal moves as unweighted edges; BFS discovers shortest hop counts.
